papers.title: A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $\epsilon$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.

papers.title: Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres
papers.abstract: This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkh\"auser (2026)).

papers.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
papers.abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

papers.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $\delta$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

papers.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
papers.abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_{\omega}$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_{\omega}$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.

papers.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
papers.abstract: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.

papers.title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=\lambda \Delta +\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\delta_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $\lambda >0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(\alpha, \theta)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $\alpha\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

papers.title: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.

papers.title: Sturm-Liouville problems on graphs with Robin boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We study characteristic functions and describe asymptotics of the eigenvalues for the spectral Sturm-Liouville problem on graphs equipped with Robin-Kirhhoff boundary conditions. Also, we show how to recover the coefficients in the Robin conditions for the quantum graphs provided the shape of the graphs and some Robin eigenvalues are known.

papers.title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter
papers.abstract: We study how the concentration of the Fourier transform changes the integrability threshold imposed by the size of its spectral support. Let $\mu$ be a positive Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $0\ne f\in L^2(\mu)$ with $f\mu$ compactly supported. Suppose that $\operatorname{supp}(f\mu)$ can be covered by $O(r^{-\alpha})$ balls of radius $r$, where $0<\alpha<n$. If the normalized Fourier ratio of $f\mu$ has decay exponent $\kappa<\frac{\alpha}{2}$, then $\widehat{f\mu}\notin L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $$2\leq p<\frac{2(n-2\kappa)}{\alpha-2\kappa},$$ and at $\kappa=\frac{\alpha}{2}$ every finite $p$ is excluded. A uniform power bound for the Fourier ratio excludes the finite critical endpoint as well. We prove that the strict range is sharp for every admissible pair $(\alpha,\kappa)$ by convolving a Salem measure with a Cantor measure whose digits are consecutive and whose bases increase, and the resulting support has Hausdorff dimension exactly $\alpha$. We also obtain necessary conditions for Fourier extension estimates and compute the Fourier ratio exponent for smooth densities on hypersurfaces whose second fundamental form has constant rank.
